newsitem.title: FRANCE: Irish PM hopeful fin mins can agree stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Irish PM hopeful fin mins can agree stability pact.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Tuesday he was hopeful that a finance ministers' meeting in Dublin on Thursday evening could solve the last issues around a stability pact before the European Union summit of Friday.
After talks with President Jacques Chirac he said he hoped Monday's meeting between Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had improved the prospects of a stability pact agreement.
"I think the principal focus will be on the Ecofin (meeting of economic and finance ministers on Thursday)," Bruton told reporters when he left the Elysee presidential palace.

"I know that these topics were discussed yesterday between president Chirac and Chancellor Kohl and I hope that these (talks) will have improved the prospects of the economic and finance meeting agreement," he said.
He said that he believed the remaining questions were "very technical and in a sense quite marginal".
"These are technical issues...those are issues that will be best or easily settled by the summit itself."
"I am hopeful that it will be possible for the Finance Ministers to do the job, I am hopeful because there is reason for hope," he said.
